definitions.gloss: chinquapin, an evergreen broadleaf tree in the beech family
definitions.explanation: An evergreen broadleaf tree (genus Castanopsis) common in warmer parts of Japan, valued for shade, its dense wood, and its small edible nuts.

examples.japanese: ⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{境内|けいだい}→境内：12095_keidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧{椎|しい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{木|き}→木：00524_ki⟧がある。
examples.english: There is a large shii tree on the shrine grounds.
Shii nuts can be roasted and eaten.

examples.japanese: {椎|しい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{常緑広葉樹|じょうりょくこうようじゅ}→常緑広葉樹：30888_jouryokukouyouju⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{一年中|いちねんじゅう}→一年中：17104_ichinenjuu⟧⟦{緑|みどり}→緑：00970_midori⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{葉|は}→葉：02241_ha⟧をつけている。
examples.english: The shii is an evergreen broadleaf tree, keeping green leaves year-round.

notes:
An evergreen broadleaf tree common in shrine groves and warm-climate forests across western and southern Japan. Its small acorn-like nuts, unlike most acorns, can be eaten roasted without the usual bitterness.
